title: Surge buffer & soft-hire priority lattice
content:
Purpose:
This working sheet sketches a compact operational framework to allocate a surge buffer (dollars + reserved GPU capacity) and to sequence 'soft hires' (contractors / temp buckets) versus full hires across 3 pricing shock scenarios. Goal is to produce a crosswalk from price volatility -> token margin erosion -> hiring triggers -> buffer drawdown rules that the finance + product + infra teams can act on quickly.

Summary (one-liner):
Create a prioritized lattice of roles and funding buckets that preserves critical latency/availability SLOs under pricing shocks while minimizing permanent headcount expansion.

Key assumptions (tunable):
- Baseline token unit cost (hosted) = $0.0008/token (Feb 2026 average).
- Reserve buffer target = 10% of monthly gross margin for Q2-Q4 2026 (expressed as cash + committed spot capacity credits).
- Soft-hire cost multiplier = 1.35x equivalent headcount (includes agency fees and ramp inefficiency).
- Vacancy rate assumption for perm roles = 8% across FY26 hiring plan.
- Latency-critical routes represent ~42% of total token spend but 60% of SLA penalty exposure.

Scenario definitions (pricing delta relative to baseline):
- Base: +0% price change (status quo)
- Mid-shock: +18% token cost -> compresses gross margin by ~7.5 percentage points
- Severe-shock: +40% token cost -> compresses gross margin by ~18 percentage points

High-level rules (procedural):
1) Buffer draw order: 1) Prefix KV cache optimization fund (infra), 2) Short-term reserved GPU credits (region-agnostic), 3) Temporary customer credit adjustments (marketing), 4) Headcount draw (last resort).
2) Soft-hire activation thresholds:
   - If monthly gross margin delta from baseline > 6% -> activate Tier 1 soft-hire bucket (SWE infra contractors, +1 product PM contractor).
   - If > 12% -> activate Tier 2 (regional SRE contractors, additional infra contractors to support queuing/batching ops).
   - If > 20% -> escalate to exec review for perm hiring or price changes.
3) Perm hiring freeze toggle: Triggered if buffer falls below 35% of target or runway reduction > 3 months. Freeze exceptions: security, compliance, and revenue-protecting roles (sales engineering for top-10 customers).

Headcount priority lattice (ranked):
- Essential perm (no substitute): SRE (latency on-call rotas), Security/Compliance, Key GTM for enterprise renewals.
- Replaceable perm / deferred: Some feature-facing SWE teams (non-latency), tooling infra not immediately critical.
- Soft-hire first-line: infra SWE contractors (batching, KV cache), SRE temp support, solutions-engineering for migration work.

Simple model snapshot (monthly):
Columns: Month | Forecast tokens (M) | Baseline token cost ($/k) | Price delta | Monthly token spend ($k) | Gross margin % | Buffer held ($k) | Buffer draw ($k) | Net buffer ($k) | Perm hires paused | Soft hires added
Example rows (text table):
Feb-2026 | 120 | 0.0008 | 0% | 96.0 | 42% | 420 | 0 | 420 | 0 | 0
Jun-2026 (mid-shock) | 150 | 0.000944 | +18% | 141.6 | 34.5% | 420 | 60 | 360 | 2 perm paused | 4 soft hired
Nov-2026 (severe) | 180 | 0.00112 | +40% | 201.6 | 24% | 420 | 170 | 250 | 6 perm paused | 9 soft hired

Notes on the arithmetic:
- Token spend = tokens * token unit cost. Values above in $k.
- Buffer draw attempts to keep runway delta under 2 months; draw capped at 60% of buffer per quarter (governance guardrail).

Governance & approval matrix:
- Up to $50k monthly buffer draw: Finance ops sign-off (fp&a lead).
- $50k-$200k: Finance + Infra SVP sign-off.
- > $200k or perm hiring beyond approved headcount plan: COO + CEO review.

Open questions / TODOs (items to resolve in follow-up):
- Agree exact measurement cadence for token cost (rolling 30d vs calendar month).
- Confirm which customer contracts allow short-term surcharge to offset pricing shocks vs those with fixed pricing. (Action: Marcus to surface top 20 contracts by token spend -> JIRA FIN-2401).
- Define 'soft-hire' contract template (duration, hourly caps, notice period) — coordinate with People Ops.
- Map which infra changes have one-time cost vs ongoing token-reduction runrate (i.e., KV cache investment expected to reduce token spend by X% ongoing).

Practical next steps (two-week sprint):
- FP&A to import last 6 months token usage by route and attach to this sheet (OWNER: Leah) — JIRA FIN-2347.
- Infra to estimate the incremental latency risk if we pause 3 SWE perm hires in Q3 (OWNER: Jonas) — deliver: short risk memo.
- Product to identify top-5 latency-critical routes and potential QoS-spec reduction options to stretch buffer (OWNER: Priya).
- Legal to vet smart-contract clauses for temporary price surcharge (OWNER: Aisha).

Appendix: quick sensitivity table (price delta vs buffer burn rate):
- +10% price -> buffer burn 18%/q 
- +20% price -> buffer burn 38%/q 
- +30% price -> buffer burn 63%/q
- +40% price -> buffer burn 95%/q
(These are heuristics derived from the current token mix and margin profile; refine with real usage data.)

Notes to self (working ideas):
- Consider 'regional reserve swaps' where low-util regions lend reserved capacity to high-demand regions for a small fee; reduces cash buffer draw.
- Pilot a 6-week 'soft-hire pool' agreement with two trusted contractors to compress ramp.
